A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with the same authors, central mechanisms and experimental framework. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison after matching relocated content.

before.justification: v1 reports original AIME and GPQA evaluations, synthetic Transformer experiments, and analyses of reasoning traces and model continuations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, updates synthetic evaluations, and adds model-capacity and looping-detector analyses.

M1.justification: The graph construction, random-walk/reset procedures, next-token objective, margin intervention and injected looping bias already appear in v1. The smaller-model sweep in v2 is an experimental ablation of the retained architecture.

E1.justification: Both versions use AIME 2024/2025, GPQA Diamond and the G(5,3), G(5,5) and G(10,5) graph tasks. The additions vary model capacity, node-label vocabulary and detector thresholds within retained task coverage.

E2.justification: Matched evaluations retain the same Qwen, OpenThinker/QwQ, Phi-4 and Llama comparison models, including instruction-tuned counterparts. The synthetic teacher and intervention comparisons are retained; the new depth sweep adds configurations for an ablation, without introducing a distinct comparison method.

E3.justification: Synthetic analyses previously specifying 500 test traces now specify 4,000. Appendix G adds 1-, 2- and 12-layer evaluations with a node-label vocabulary of 50, versus 30 in other experiments. Appendix A.3 adds detector settings (10,10), (10,20) and (10,40). The principal training recipe and open-model evaluation protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix G adds a controlled depth ablation testing capacity as a source of hardness. Appendix A.3 extends detector sensitivity testing and inspects false positives. Appendix E adds temporal-correlation measurements for the existing combined-mechanism experiments. These are focused extensions of the retained analyses.

E5.justification: Repeated-continuation counts for open-model evaluations and case studies remain unchanged, with no new seed, confidence-interval or significance-test reporting. Larger synthetic test sets concern E3. The new 5% support cutoff restricts displayed mean curves without changing their averaging formula.

E6.justification: Synthetic numerical results change alongside the larger reported test samples: reset overestimation changes from 94% of positions with mean about 0.35 to about 91% with mean about 0.33; top-child persistence changes from 96.7% to 98.7%. v2 also adds capacity, 10-gram sensitivity and combined-mechanism correlation results. The principal qualitative findings remain stable.

T1.justification: Proposition 1 becomes Proposition 3.1 with the same assumptions, conclusion and KKT proof. The token-chunk probability argument moves to Appendix C, and the combined-mechanism derivations are retained. No new formal result or substantive proof revision appears.

C1.justification: Both versions identify learning errors, hardness-induced risk aversion and temporally correlated errors as explanations for looping, and describe temperature as an incomplete remedy. v2 gives the confidence-buildup catalyst greater prominence, but v1 already claims and demonstrates it.

C2.justification: Section 6.1 adds specific limitations concerning semantic action identification, probability estimation and interacting mechanisms when transferring synthetic insights to real models. Section 4.1 argues that second-ranked-child persistence cannot be explained solely by reinforcing sampled actions. v2 also explains high-temperature accuracy losses and false positives from permissive looping detectors.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link and documents the new capacity study's parameter counts and node-label vocabulary. It corrects the stated Phi-4 source teacher from o4-mini to o3-mini. The principal Transformer training details are relocated to Appendix D without substantive changes.

R1.justification: v2 adds Kalimeris et al. and Rahaman et al. to support easier-function learning biases, and Sinha et al. for self-conditioning. It removes several supporting references, including Su and Collier and some hardness citations. The central positioning relative to text degeneration and star-graph reasoning remains stable.

P1.justification: The main narrative is extensively condensed and reorganized. Detailed traces move into a unified Appendix B, training details and implications move to Appendix D, and the main text summarizes both examples. The catalyst receives its own section, and the discussion gains a dedicated limitations subsection.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 2 and Figure 21, relocates the greedy-decoding bar chart to Appendix A, and redisplays a catalyst panel as main-text Figure 5. Several plots are resized or redrawn. Figures 17 and 19 restrict average curves to indices reached by at least 5% of traces; most existing displays are retained.

improvement.justification: The capacity ablation provides additional support for an existing explanation, while Table 2's false-positive analysis better motivates the looping detector. More specific synthetic-to-real limitations, clearer organization and a code-access link improve interpretability and transparency. These are useful refinements; the central mechanisms, proof and real-model evidence remain largely unchanged.
